title: The leaf blower
summary: The leaf blower in R.E.P.O. is a tool with a fan rather than a weapon: the game gives it its own blowing particles, its own loop sounds, and battery use that rises when it hits something.
body: The blower is its own item. The game ships it with a fan and its own particles rather than as a reskinned gun, which is why it moves things instead of damaging them.
It blows visibly. The blower has its own blow particles and a grab area of its own, which is why what it does to an object can be seen rather than only felt.
It runs on a battery. The blower carries a battery drain rate of its own, so it is one of the tools that makes charge worth carrying.
Hitting something costs more. There is a separate drain for hitting a monster, which is why using it as a weapon runs the battery down faster than using it as a tool.
It announces itself. The blower has an on sound, an off sound, and a start and end for its blowing loop, so you can hear whether it is running.
It can hurt. The blower carries a hurt volume of its own, so it is not purely a tool even though it is built to move things.
What this entry does not tell you: how far it reaches, how much damage it does, or how long a battery lasts. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The blower is its own item with a fan rather than being a reskinned gun.
It has its own blowing particles and a grab area.
It runs on a battery at a rate of its own.
Hitting a monster drains the battery separately.
It has on and off sounds and a blowing loop with a start and an end.

facts.claim: It carries a hurt volume of its own.
